recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-23839 unless the work group makes a new decision about Annotation.author[x] or handles a separate editorial cleanup.
issue_request: FHIR-23839 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core datatypes clarification, raised against STU3 and applied for R5, asking datatypes#annotation to encourage implementers to avoid Annotation.authorString and use Annotation.authorReference.display because Annotation is normative and the choice could not be removed.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied by commit a705329af6cbb66189916ad41320f5368d39d654, later merged by 1959e232f5cf79644c67ef10b912a775010ee1a2 / HL7/fhir#2222. That commit reorganized the Annotation notes in source/datatypes.html and added the current SHOULD guidance to use Annotation.authorReference.display instead of Annotation.authorString.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists Annotation as an active datatype and normative artifact, and source/datatypes/annotation.xml still defines Annotation.author[x] as a Reference-or-string choice. FHIR-I minutes corroborate the Persuasive 3-0-0 vote. Related Annotation author decisions already audited on the combined branch, including FHIR-16965 and FHIR-19691, affect other author targets but do not alter this authorString guidance.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/datatypes.html already contains the requested guidance; the duplicated words in the sentence are editorial-only and do not change implementer understanding for this reconciliation.

related_jiras.note: Earlier Annotation author/text issue already audited on the combined branch; it rejected Group as an Annotation author target and does not change the FHIR-23839 authorString guidance.
